unspecified.behavior: The drawing margin (half the scroller's height) is computed once, when the IntersectionObserver is created (dependencies `[firstRatio, numPages]`), and is never recomputed when the window is resized or the phone sheet changes height.

scores.reason: After the reader resizes the window or raises the sheet, pages are pre-drawn with a margin sized for the old height, so more white faces flash briefly while scrolling.

Confirmed at PdfPagesPanel.tsx:139-157. The rootMargin uses the scroller's visible height when the observer is created, and the dependencies are only [firstRatio, state.numPages]. Resizing the window, or a phone sheet that is still moving when the rail mounts, leaves the pre-draw margin too large or too small. The only effect is that thumbnails start drawing a little earlier or later than intended; pages inside the visible box still intersect and are drawn.

counted.reason: After the reader resizes the window or raises the sheet, pages are pre-drawn with a margin sized for the old height, so more white faces flash briefly while scrolling.

unspecified.behavior: Cells in `drawing` (entered the margin but not yet rendered) do not count toward the 120-page cap. Only `drawn` cells are evicted, so a fast scroll can mount more `<Page>` renders than the cap for a while.

scores.reason: Fast scrolling through a long PDF can briefly hold more than 120 rasters in memory. Nothing visible changes.

Confirmed at PdfPagesPanel.tsx:197-219 and 311-319. The cap check reads only `drawn.size`, and an `entered` page leaves only through eviction or failure. A fast scroll through a 200+ page PDF can therefore mount more than 120 <Page> renders at once. The user may see a short CPU or memory spike and slower drawing, and the effect trims the drawn set back to 120 once those renders finish.

unspecified.behavior: A page enters `entered` when it intersects the extended box and only leaves through eviction or failure (PdfPagesPanel.tsx:148, 218, 260). Scrolling past a page without stopping still commits it to a full render.

scores.reason: Flinging the rail of a long PDF queues renders for every page passed over, so the pages the user lands on can be drawn later than they would otherwise be.
